_comment: WC2026 QUARTER-FINAL (QF99: winner of Brazil-Norway vs winner of Mexico-England). KNOCKOUT: no draw -- level after 90' -> extra time -> penalties, so the deliverable is who ADVANCES. Winner meets the Argentina-Switzerland winner in the semi-finals (M102). Nominal bracket orientation is Norway (home, feeder 93) vs England (away, feeder 94) on a neutral venue; modelled here with ENGLAND as home for clarity (the favourite) -- immaterial on a neutral venue; the web app flips the orientation. Routes: England WON Group L (4-2 Croatia, 0-0 Ghana, 2-0 Panama; rating 91), beat DR Congo 2-1 in the R32 (Kane brace, from 1-0 down) and won the 3-2 thriller vs host Mexico in the R16. KANE IS FIRING, but England CONCEDES in almost every game (2 Croatia, 1 Congo, 2 Mexico) -- a real attack with a leaky-ish defence. Norway finished 2nd in Group I (4-1 Iraq, 3-1 Senegal, 1-4 France; rating 81), won 2-1 vs Ivory Coast (93' winner) and then pulled the shock of the round: ELIMINATED BRAZIL 2-1 with a HAALAND BRACE from a 26% advancement position. Class gap ~10 (91 vs 81) -> England the clear favourite, BUT this is the BTTS rule's ELITE-STRIKER EXCEPTION in its purest form: (1) Norway has HAALAND, in red-hot form (brace vs Brazil) -- do NOT hard-trim (lambda 1.15, the same nuance that was vindicated vs Brazil); (2) England's defence is leaky (conceded in 4 of 5) -> Norway scores; (3) England's own games run HIGH (4-2, 2-1, 3-2 -- and the Mexico-England lesson: don't anchor a low total against England). -> an OPEN, higher-scoring tie: BTTS-YES 57%, Over 2.5 55%, xG 2.90. England favoured (their attack vs Norway's leaky GA-6 defence), but Norway's upset equity is REAL and at the UPPER end of its range (the Brazil-Norway lesson: an elite-striker underdog is where the favourite's ~35% elimination tail actually fires -- they have already done it once). Home = England (nominal; neutral venue; bracket shows Norway as home). Cards not modelled (referee TBD).

_postmatch.result: England 2-1 Norway AFTER EXTRA TIME (1-1 at 90'). England advance to the semi-finals (where they meet the Argentina-Switzerland winner). Norway's run ends in extra time; England survive the Haaland test.
_postmatch.model_1x2: England 50.6 / Draw 25.1 / Norway 24.2 (MEDIUM, 90'); advancement England 64.9 / Norway 35.1
_postmatch.verdict: As close to a perfect forecast as this model produces. England advanced as the 64.9% pick (✅). The 90' result was 1-1 -- the MODAL scoreline (11.8%) -- sending it to extra time, the branch I priced FAT (25.1%, among the higher of the QFs) precisely because this pairing was open-but-even. BTTS-Yes (57.2% lean) landed: Norway scored on England's leaky defence exactly as the elite-striker exception prescribed (Haaland's side has now scored in every game). And England's advancement decomposition worked as designed: reg 50.6% did NOT fire (draw at 90'), but the ET branch (8.2% of their 64.9%) did -- the favourite's class told in the extra 30 minutes against a tiring underdog. Every layer of the forecast (side, modal scoreline, ET-heavy structure, BTTS, the open texture) was correct. Norway's upper-range 35.1% was honest: they took the eventual winner to extra time, a kick or two from another upset.
_postmatch.lesson: The layered advancement forecast (reg + ET + pens) proves its worth: a favourite at ~65% with a fat ET branch is EXPECTED to sometimes need extra time -- that is not a scare, it is the priced path (contrast a naive 1X2 read, which would score the 90' draw as a 'miss'). The elite-striker exception is now decisively validated: Norway/Haaland scored in EVERY game including vs Brazil and England -- never BTTS-No a side with a world-class striker. And the England profile holds: real attack, leaky defence, games always involve goals at both ends (BTTS-Yes in 5 of their 6). For the semi vs Argentina or Switzerland: England games run open and deep; Argentina games run chaotic -- an Argentina-England semi would be a goals fest by both profiles.
